questions.answer: This equation is already separated because the right-hand side depends only on \(x\). Integrate both sides with respect to \(x\): \(y=\int2x\,dx\). This gives \(y=x^2+C\). Therefore the general solution is \(y=x^2+C\).

Separate the variables: \(\frac{1}{y}\,dy=x\,dx\), assuming \(y\ne0\). Integrate both sides to get \(\ln|y|=x^2/2+C\). Exponentiating gives \(y=Ae^{x^2/2}\). The constant \(A=0\) includes the zero solution, so this is the general solution.

Separate variables: \(y^{-2}\,dy=dx\), for \(y\ne0\). Integrate to get \(-y^{-1}=x+C\). Rearranging gives \(1/y=C_1-x\), so \(y=1/(C_1-x)\). The constant solution \(y=0\) is also a solution and should be included separately.
Separate variables: \(\frac{1}{y}\,dy=3\,dx\). Integrate to get \(\ln|y|=3x+C\), so \(y=Ae^{3x}\). Apply \(y(0)=4\): \(4=Ae^0=A\). Therefore \(y=4e^{3x}\).

Separate variables: \(\frac{1}{1+y^2}\,dy=x\,dx\). Integrate both sides: \(\arctan y=x^2/2+C\). Apply tangent to both sides to solve for \(y\): \(y=\tan(x^2/2+C)\). Therefore the general solution is \(y=\tan(x^2/2+C)\).

Separate variables by multiplying by \(y\): \(y\,dy=x^2\,dx\). Integrate both sides: \(y^2/2=x^3/3+C\). Multiply by \(2\): \(y^2=2x^3/3+C_1\). Thus \(y=\pm\sqrt{2x^3/3+C_1}\), on intervals where the square root is defined.

Multiply both sides by \(e^y\) to separate variables: \(e^y\,dy=e^x\,dx\). Integrate: \(e^y=e^x+C\). Taking natural logarithms gives \(y=\ln(e^x+C)\), where the logarithm requires \(e^x+C>0\) on the interval considered.

Separate variables: \(\frac{1}{y(1-y)}\,dy=dt\). Use partial fractions \(\frac{1}{y(1-y)}=\frac{1}{y}+\frac{1}{1-y}\). Integrate to get \(\ln|y|-\ln|1-y|=t+C\), so \(\ln\left|\frac{y}{1-y}\right|=t+C\). For \(0<y<1\), \(\frac{y}{1-y}=Ae^t\), hence \(y=\frac{Ae^t}{1+Ae^t}\).

Separate variables by multiplying by \(y+2\): \((y+2)\,dy=(x+1)\,dx\). Integrate both sides: \(y^2/2+2y=x^2/2+x+C\). This implicit equation is the general solution. Multiplying by \(2\) gives the equivalent form \(y^2+4y=x^2+2x+C_1\).

questions.prompt: Solve the initial value problem \(dy/dx=x/y\), \(y(0)=2\), assuming \(y>0\).
questions.answer: Separate variables: \(y\,dy=x\,dx\). Integrate: \(y^2/2=x^2/2+C\), so \(y^2=x^2+C_1\). Use \(y(0)=2\): \(4=0+C_1\), so \(C_1=4\). Since \(y>0\), take the positive root: \(y=\sqrt{x^2+4}\).
